title: CID Special Agent
raw_text:
8-311A. Military Occupational Specialty 311A--CID Special Agent
   a. Licensing/certification. AR 195-3.
   b. Prerequisites. AR 195-3 and DA Cir 601 series.
   c. MOS 311A. MOS 311A is an accession MOS. The enlisted feeder MOS is 31D. All
applicants must apply for acceptance into the Special Agent program IAW the requirements of
195-3.
   d. Restrictions. No record of conviction by special or general courts-martial or civilian courts of
offenses listed in AR 27-10 (Military Justice), chapter 24 or otherwise required to register as a
sexual offender under AR 27-10, chapter 24.
   e. Associated SQI.
        (1) 0--No special qualifications.
        (2) 8--Instructor.
        (3) K--Polygraph Examiner.
        (4) P--Parachutist.
        (5) T--Transition (personnel only).
        (6) Z--Research, Development, Test, and Evaluation Technician.
   f. Associated ASI. (Note: Refer to table 6-6 (Listing of universal ASI’s associated with all
MOS)).
        (1) P2---Protective Services Specialist.
        (2) P7—Digital Forensic Examiner (DFE)).
        (3) P8—Basic Special Victims Investigator (BSVI) (personnel only).
        (4) Q6--Protection Cell Operations (personnel only) (Effective 202410).
        (5) Q8—Senior Special Victims Investigator (SSVI) (personnel only).
   g. Qualifications.
        (1) WO1 must--
              (a) Be a U.S. citizen. Qualify for security eligibility of TS.
              (b) Meet the qualifications outlined in AR 195-3 (paragraph 2-2), (Acceptance,
Accreditation and Release of U.S. Army Criminal Investigation Command Personnel).
              (c) Be accredited by the Director, Army CID, as required by AR 195-3.
              (d) Must have completed Warrant Officer Candidate Course (WOCC) and the
Warrant Officer Basic Course (WOBC).
        (2) CW2 must--
              (a) Meet qualifications described in paragraph g(1).
              (b) Complete the Warrant Officer Intermediate Course (WOIC) Distant Learning (DL)
and CID (WOIC–DL)
        (3) CW3 must--
              (a) Meet qualifications described in paragraph g(2).
              (b) Complete the Warrant Officer Advance Course (WOAC) and follow-on CID
(WOAC).
        (4) CW4 must--
             (a) Meet qualifications described in paragraph g(3).
             (b) Complete the Warrant Officer Senior Course (WOSC) and follow-on CID WOSC.
        (5) CW5 must--
             (a) Meet qualifications described in paragraph g(4).
             (b) Complete the Warrant Officer Master Course (WOMC) as required by nominative
position.
   h. Duties.
        (1) WO1/CW2 must--
              (a) Investigate felony and other significant crime of Army interest as defined by
regulations, military, and federal law.
              (b) Plans, organizes, conducts, and supervises overt and covert investigations.
              (c) Examines and processes crime scenes.
              (d) Collects, preserves, and evaluates physical evidence for scientific examination by
laboratories and use in judicial proceedings.
              (e) Obtains and executes arrest and search warrants.
              (f) Conducts raids and task force operations.
                (g) Interviews and interrogates victims, witnesses, suspects, and subjects and obtain
written statements executed under oath.
               (h) Develops, evaluates, and manages informants and other sources of criminal
intelligence.
               (i) Represents the Army's interest in investigations conducted collaterally with the
Department of Defense, Department of Justice, and other federal, state, and local investigative
agencies.
               (j) Maintains close working relationships with attorneys of the Staff Judge Advocate
and the United States Attorney's Office, and testify at Courts-Martial, Federal District Court, and
other judiciary tribunals.
               (k) Writes, reviews, and approves technical investigative reports.
               (l) Conducts and supervises technical surveys of Army elements and activities which
analyze and detect on-going crime, and recommends actions to prevent crime which could result
in significant economic loss and reduced combat effectiveness.
               (m) Conducts personnel security vulnerability assessments for designated senior
Army officials.
               (n) Provides personnel security for designated Department of Defense executives,
visiting foreign officials, and other key officials.
               (o) Performs hostage negotiations
               (p) Perform duties as Digital Forensics Examiner, Polygraph Examiner, Field Office
Tactics Advisor, Field Training Agent, Tech Agent, Forensic Science Consultant.
         (2) CW3 must--
               (a) Performs duties described in paragraph h(1).
               (b) Provides technical guidance and direction to subordinate investigative units.
               (c) Trains new Special Agents on duties described in paragraph h(1).
               (d) Performs duties as Branch Chief, Training Developer, Instructor/SGL at DACID
Training Academy, Assistant Detail Leader, Senior Field Training Agent, Senior Digital Forensic
Examinaer.
         (3) CW4 must—
               (a) Performs duties described in paragraph h(1-2).
               (b) Supervises investigative case management and overall investigative operations.
               (c) Supervises the technical performance of subordinate personnel in related job
skills.
               (d) Performs duties as the Senior Supervisory Agent, Detail Leader, and Detailed IG,
         (4) CW5 must--
               (a) Performs duties described in paragraph h(1-3).
               (b)
               (c) Supervises and provides guidance and technical advice to subordinate
investigative units or other staff elements.
               (d) Performs duties as Liaison Officer for Army Commands., Chief, DACID Training
Academy.
               (e) Performs duties as the Warrant Officer Advisor to the Director, Army CID.
    i. Physical demands category, grading and position titles.
         (1) Physical Demands Category (PDC) – Moderate (Gold).
         (2) A physical profile of 222221.
         (3) Normal color vision.
         (4) Table 8-311A-1. Physical requirements.
         (5) A minimum OPAT score of Standing Long Jump (LJ) - 0120 cm, seated Power Throw
(PT) - 0350 cm, Strength Deadlift (SD) - 0120 lbs., and Interval Aerobic Run (IR) - 0036 shuttles
in Physical Demands Category in Moderate (Gold).
         (6) The following grades are used to code positions into one of four definable skill levels:
W2 equals WO1/CW2; W3 equals CW3; W4 equals CW4; and W5 equals CW5. The grades are
listed in the following standards of grade tables:
              (a) Table 8-311A-2. Standards of grade TOE/MTOE.
              (b) Table 8-311A-3. Standards of grade TDA.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
